key_insight: FT-Weave is a real-time, stage-aware FTQC compiler that coordinates preparation, routing, assignment, and corrections to keep fault-tolerant quantum workloads moving under stochastic hardware behavior.
engineering_relevance: It shows that runtime orchestration, not just static parallelism, is critical for achieving high throughput on reconfigurable fault-tolerant quantum architectures.
method: Adapts scheduling to live resource availability instead of assuming fixed factory throughput.
Jointly manages resource preparation, teleportation routing, logical execution, and correction handling.
Targets two neutral-atom FTQC designs: transversal STAR and T-state cultivation.
evidence_signal: On the evaluated hardware and latency model, FT-Weave reached up to 3× speedup over a baseline compiler on two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model simulations.
watch_item: Fine-grained asynchrony can increase routing contention and shrink optimization windows, so more concurrency does not always translate into shorter execution time.
paper_title: FT-Weave: Real-Time Compilation Framework for Reconfigurable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Architectures
